text:
carlos: Ran the kernel sweep across H100 / A100 / L40S this morning. Found a pretty nasty oscillation pattern on L40S for long seqs + small batches.

carlos: Quick notes: seq sweep: [512,1024,2048,4096], bsz sweep: [1,2,4,16]. Using runtime v2.9.1 with the new kernel-selector heuristic (sha: a1b2c3d).

maria: Can you paste the raw numbers? curious if it’s a kernel fallback or mem thrash. :thinking:

carlos: Sure — trimmed to relevant rows. Command we ran:

```
./bench_attn --device L40S,H100,A100 --seqs 512,1024,2048,4096 --bszs 1,2,4,16 --model t5-xxl --runs 5
```

Perf summary (ms/step, median):
H100: 512/1: 8.1, 1024/1: 12.5, 2048/1: 22.3, 4096/1: 44.8
A100: 512/1: 9.6, 1024/1: 14.2, 2048/1: 26.0, 4096/1: 50.1
L40S: 512/1: 11.0, 1024/1: 18.5, 2048/1: 39.2, 4096/1: 18.9 <-- NOTE: drops back down on 4096

carlos: For L40S with bsz=2: 2048 -> 41.7ms, 4096 -> 19.4ms. With bsz=4 the 4096 point looks stable at 17–20ms. So the weird thing is only when batch is very small (1 or 2) and seq hits 4096 we see the latency drop, but at 2048 it's high. Oscillation across seqs, not monotonic.

aj: That smells like a prefetch/kv cache interaction — maybe paged attention kernel is being chosen for some lengths but falls back to fused/paged combo mid-stream. Any profiler traces?

carlos: I captured a perftrace and nvtx for the problematic runs. Relevant excerpt (L40S, bsz=1):

```
[2058ms] kernel_selector: chose paged_fused_attn (reason: mem_est>threshold)
[2060ms] kv_cache: miss_rate=0.23, prefetch_window=128
[2065ms] memcpy: repeated small copies (4x) -> stall 120ms
[2200ms] fallback: swapped to flash_variant_v2
[2210ms] kv_cache: eviction spike -> memcopy bursts
[2220ms] step_complete: 39.2ms
```

carlos: For 4096 the selector picked flash_variant_v3 up-front (different tiling), no repeated small copies, so throughput looks better. So the heuristic is flipping to paged when mem_est crosses a threshold around 3.0GB, but that path has a prefetch pattern that thrashes the L40S memcpy bandwidth at small batch sizes.

devon: Which commit introduced the threshold change? I remember we bumped mem_est threshold in the selector to avoid OOMs on A100. Might be the culprit.

aj: I can repro locally with a tiny repro: seq=2048,bsz=1,model t5-xxl and `--kv-simulate-miss-rate 0.22` to force the branch. If perf matches, we can add a guard to prefer flash_variant when bsz <= 2 even if mem_est is high.

maria: +1 for a simple guard. Also we should record cold_kv_rate metric in the console so rollouts can be tied to real traffic. Right now we only expose average kv hit rate, not cold -> that would have flagged this.

perf-bot: Canary results posted: https://ci.internal.redwood/canaries/2923456789 — shows 3/5 canaries with L40S regression on seq=2048.

devon: OK plan: 1) short-term patch: kernel-selector: if bsz<=2 and gpu_family==L40S prefer flash_variant fallback override; 2) instrument cold_kv_rate and prefetch small-copy counts; 3) rollback threshold commit if patch fails.

aj: I’ll open a small PR for the selector guard and a unit test that simulates kv miss spikes. PR will include a flag `--prefer-flash-small-batch` and default it true for L40S.

carlos: Added a repro script to /bench/repro/2923456789_repro.sh and pinned the exact binary used. Leaving it in the thread for anyone who wants to run:

```
# repro
python repro_attn.py --device L40S --seq 2048 --bsz 1 --model t5-xxl --kv-miss 0.22
```

maria: Great. Can we get a quick dashboard panel? I want to see cold_kv_rate + kernel_choice histogram per host for last 24h. If the rollout just hit a few hosts we can rollback fast.

devon: I’ll add panels and a short alert if cold_kv_rate>0.15 and median_latency(seq=2048,bsz=1) > baseline*1.3.

carlos: Thanks. If anyone reproduces differently ping me. I think this proves we need kernel-selection-aware of batch size and kv access pattern, not just mem_est.

aj: Running the PR tests now, will tag you @carlos when green. :thumbsup:
